Subject: Post-call: Northbridge residency & PII handling — follow-ups

Hi Elena — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and items we promised to follow up on from the discovery: 

1) High-level ask: confirm whether Northbridge requires strict country-level data residency (i.e., primary storage and backups must remain in EU for EU customers, APAC for APAC customers) or if a regional/sovereignty model (data anchored to region with encrypted cross-region backups) is acceptable.

2) PII scope: you mentioned insurance claimants + agent notes (names, SSN partials, policy numbers). Can you confirm which classes of data you regard as regulated PII vs. low-sensitivity metadata?

3) Retention & deletion: requested retention windows (primary vs. logs) and any legal hold needs — you said 7 years for claims but we should get exact retention rules per line of business.

4) Logging/audit: level of audit/logging required for API calls, token-level tracing, and whether you need access to raw request payloads for e-discovery.

5) Failover/backups: preference between warm-standby in a secondary region vs. active-active (read-only replica) for recovery point/objectives. Also how quickly backups must be geo-immutable.

Next steps from our side: we will provide a concise answers sheet for the questionnaire items, a region-residency factsheet, and a suggested contract clause for data residency and backups. I've attached the factsheet and would appreciate the completed questionnaire you mentioned so we can map answers to controls.

Proposed timeline: 48 business hours for the initial answers + factsheet; follow-up call next week to validate.

Attachments: redwood-region-factsheet.pdf (summary of residency behaviors), compliance-slides (link in email).

Best,

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications and I've attached our standardized security questionnaire (PDF). Please see inline answers/requests below: 

- Residency model: For EU customers we require primary storage and backups to remain within the EU. For APAC we require data to be stored in APAC; however we are open to encrypted, immutable backups in a secondary jurisdiction if (a) backups are encrypted with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and (b) we can control access via RBAC and audit logs.

- PII scope: confirmed regulated: full name, national ID (SSN/NI), date of birth, policy numbers linked to claims. Agent notes sometimes include PHI (health-related statements) — flag for higher controls.

- Retention: claims data default 7 years, agent notes 10 years for some products — we'll attach a retention table in the completed questionnaire.

- Logging: we require audit trails for all administrative access, full request/response logging for e-discovery (retained for 2 years), and an immutable access log for security events (5 years).

- Failover/backups: preference is warm-standby in a regional cluster for faster recovery. Cross-region failover is acceptable for disaster recovery only. Backups must be retained according to the retention table and marked immutable for 90 days post-write.

Please review the attached questionnaire (Northbridge_Security_Questionnaire_v1.pdf) and return with Redwood's mapped controls. Also include the default contractual language you propose for residency/backups and any KMS options.

Happy to hop on a quick 30-minute call next Tue 10–12 PT if that helps.

Best,

Thanks Marissa — looping you all together. Below is a concise draft we can send to Elena and the questionnaire mapping (high level). I attached our region factsheet for their reference and a short draft clause — please review.

--- Suggested email to Elena (short):
Hi Elena — thanks for the questionnaire and clarifications. Attached is a control mapping (XLS summary) and our region factsheet. In short: Redwood supports country/region anchoring for EU and APAC primary storage; for cross-region backups we offer an encrypted, customer-managed-key (CMK) option with strict RBAC and audit logging. Backups can be marked immutable for a customer-controlled retention window. We will include the proposed contractual language below and are happy to review with legal.

--- High-level control mapping (to include in XLS):
- Primary storage locality: supported (EU, APAC, US) — controls: region pinning + geo-fencing + separate metadata partitions.
- Backups: encrypted-at-rest, optional CMK (customer HSM/KMS), stored in specified secondary region when requested.
- Logging/audit: admin access logs retained 5 years (configurable), request/response logs retained up to 2 years (configurable per contract).
- E-discovery: support for export of raw request payloads under customer-admin permission and DSAR workflows.

--- Draft contractual paragraph (for legal review):
"Redwood shall maintain customer data at the region(s) designated by Customer (the "Designated Regions"). For EU and APAC Designated Regions, Redwood will ensure primary storage and its routine backups are geographically located within the applicable Designated Region. At Customer's request, Redwood may maintain encrypted backups in a secondary region for disaster recovery, provided such backups are encrypted with Customer-provided or Customer-managed keys (CMK) and access is restricted via RBAC and audited. Redwood will retain immutable backup markers for the period specified in the applicable Order Form. Any cross-border transfer necessary for disaster recovery will be performed in accordance with applicable law and subject to Customer's instructions."

Attachments to include when we send: redwood-region-factsheet.pdf, control-mapping-NB-2029-0034.xlsx (we will generate), suggested-clause.docx

Monica — please flag any legal concerns. Rishi — if you can attach the XLS mapping and a short diagram of warm-standby vs active-active topology, that'd be ideal. I can send to Elena once we finalize.
